chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-Bakhtari from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

"The impotent man is given a year from the day his wife refers his condition to the judge; if he becomes capable, [the marriage continues], otherwise they are separated. If she agrees to stay with him and then seeks the option of separation after that, the option has fallen and she has no option."

And the more preferred opinion in my view is to act upon the report we narrated last, that if impotence occurs after consummation, she does not have the option of separation and is tested according to what the hadith of Isma'il ibn Ayyash contains, and according to what the hadith of Ghiyath al-Tabari contains, that if he has intercourse with her once, they are not separated, and the man is not returned for a defect, and other such reports that we have presented.

key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: The option/right of separation (for the wife)
key_terms.الْعِنِّينُ: The impotent man (one unable to consummate marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a wife if her husband is impotent?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the judicial procedure for 'unnah (impotence), granting the wife the right to refer the matter to a judge for a one-year probationary period. The scholar notes a nuanced debate regarding whether the wife retains the right of *khiyar* (option to dissolve) if impotence occurs post-consummation, ultimately favoring the view that she does not, as the husband is not penalized for the defect.
